skill.name: content-system-product-proposal
skill.title: Product proposal
skill.description: Argues, with evidence, why one product solution is the best, so the product owner can review, comment and decide before anything is built.

purpose: Let the product owner decide before anything is built. The proposal argues why the chosen solution is the best, backs every claim and is complete without padding.
when_to_use: A new Agnes capability or a change to one, reviewed by the product owner before design or build starts.
when_not_to_use: A bug fix, a data report (data-report) or a runbook.

method.instruction: Who has the problem, what they do today, what it costs, one real example with its source.
Read the code, docs and running app. Every claim gets a file path or link. Label what you could not inspect.
Read how 3 to 5 competitors solve it, from their own docs. Link each source.
At least two alternatives, including doing nothing, on the same criteria.
Have GPT Astra review the draft; address or rebut every finding.

lead.guidance: Max 3 sentences: what changes, for whom, which decision is needed by when.

sections.title: What changed
sections.answers: What differs from the previous version, and why?
sections.guidance: Changed sections and decisions, each with its reason and the comment it answers.

sections.title: Summary and decisions needed
sections.answers: What is proposed and what must the owner decide?
sections.guidance: Proposal in 3 to 5 bullets, then each decision as one line with the recommendation.

sections.title: The problem
sections.answers: Who is hurt, how, and what does it cost today?
sections.guidance: Who, situation, cost in numbers, one real example with source (ticket, Slack thread, session).

sections.title: Goals and non-goals
sections.answers: What must change, and what is out of scope?
sections.guidance: Goals as user outcomes; non-goals explicit so silence promises nothing.

sections.title: Principles
sections.answers: Which rules must the solution respect?
sections.guidance: 3 to 6 rules, each with a short name and one plain line; refer to them by name, never by number.

sections.title: How we know it worked
sections.guidance: Outcome checks a user would notice, each with baseline, target and a date within the delivery phases; guardrails that must not get worse.

sections.title: Current state in Agnes
sections.answers: How does it work today, for users and in code?
sections.guidance: User flow today, code locations as repo paths, annotated screenshots of the real app.

sections.title: Research and competition
sections.answers: How do others solve it, and where is Agnes?
sections.guidance: Competitors' approaches, a comparison table, Agnes now vs after each phase; every claim linked.

sections.title: Proposal
sections.answers: What will users do and see?
sections.guidance: User journey, behaviour, states, limits, errors; mockups labelled Concept.

sections.title: Alternatives and why this one
sections.answers: Why is this option better than the others?
sections.guidance: Do nothing plus at least one real option, same criteria, argued verdict.

sections.title: Decisions
sections.guidance: A meeting brief per decision: what it is about (today, what changes, why now); one example shown in every option; options table with Pros, Cons, Change later, Who does this (sourced); recommendation with its reason; a form. No paths or config keys.

sections.title: Architecture impact
sections.guidance: C4 containers and components touched, a diagram, and a surfaces matrix (Tests, Docs, Frontend, API, CLI, MCP, external services) with yes/no and why.

sections.title: Delivery plan
sections.answers: How is it built, released and checked?
sections.guidance: Phases with ambitious dates at AI-agent build speed (days, not months), none waiting for decisions; what works for users after each. Switch, dependencies, risks, given/when/then acceptance.

sections.title: Second opinion
sections.answers: What did GPT Astra find, and what was done?
sections.guidance: Each finding with its resolution: changed (where) or rebutted (why).

sections.title: Glossary
sections.answers: What do the new or redefined terms mean?
sections.guidance: Every new or redefined term, matching GLOSSARY.md.

sections.title: Sources
sections.guidance: Numbered list: title, link or repo path, date or commit; only what was actually read.

sections.title: Appendix: technical detail
sections.answers: What detail supports the text without changing it?
sections.guidance: Collapsible: data models, API shapes, raw research notes.

hierarchy: Lead, summary and decisions carry the document. Detail goes to the appendix; decisive caveats stay in the main text.

rules: Bilingual: the full document in Czech and English with the same structure; Czech is shown first. Budgets apply per language.
Plain words, short sentences. Numbers over adjectives.
Explain every number, unit and term on first use (what 180 s measures, what a turn is); no slogans or abstract policy wording.
Every claim about Agnes cites a repo path or link; every claim about a competitor cites a source link.
Mark each consequential claim verified, inferred or unverified.
Label every mockup or generated image Concept.
Every commitment names an owner (default: the requester) and a date.
No filler, no hype, no empty section. Every sentence changes what the reader knows or decides.
Each visual has a takeaway caption and a text equivalent; never colour alone.

visuals: Annotated screenshots of today, a competitor comparison table with a position chart, a C4 diagram of what changes, a phase timeline.
checklist: Lead: what changes, for whom, which decision.
The problem has one real example with a source.
Each metric has a baseline, a target and a date.
Every Agnes claim has a path or link; every competitor claim a source.
At least two alternatives, including doing nothing.
Each decision card follows the meeting-brief structure and has a form.
The surfaces matrix covers Tests, Docs, Frontend, API, CLI, MCP and external services.
A rollout switch and given/when/then acceptance examples.
Every Astra finding is addressed or rebutted.
Czech and English say the same thing.
